extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and patent office officials (United Kingdom)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and legal standards governing application for, examination, acceptance, amendment, opposition, sealing, term, enforcement, revocation, compulsory licences, extensions, and ancillary procedures for patents in the UK (Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act 1883 and related provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voidness of general monopolies and grants
rubrics_metrics.description: All grants and monopolies, and the benefit of any penal laws or of power to dispense with the law, or to compound for forfeiture, are contrary to the laws of the realm and shall be utterly void and of none effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the general principle that monopolies are void except as otherwise provided (e.g., specific patent exceptions). Background contextual statute explaining limitation on royal monopolies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory exception for patents of new manufactures (fourteen years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters patents and grants of privilege for the term of fourteen years or under for the sole working or making of any manner of new manufactures may be granted to the true and first inventor or inventors, provided they are not contrary to the law nor mischievous to the state by raising prices, hurting trade, or generally inconvenient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fourteen years is to be computed from date of the first letters patent or grant; this is the key statutory carve-out permitting limited exclusive rights to new manufactures under conditions of not being contrary to law or harmful to public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may apply for a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person, whether a British subject or not, may make an application for a patent; two or more persons may make a joint application and a patent may be granted to them jointly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirms entitlement to apply is open to foreigners and joint applicants; informs eligibility of applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and lodging of application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent must be made in the form set forth in the First Schedule or in such other form as may be prescribed, and must be left at or sent by post to the Patent Office in the prescribed manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must follow prescribed/formal paperwork and filing channels (rule compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of possession and claim to be true and first inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must contain a declaration to the effect that the applicant is in possession of an invention, and that he (or one or more joint applicants) claims to be the true and first inventor(s) of the invention, and must be accompanied by either a provisional or complete specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaration is a required component of the application; accompaniment by specification (provisional or complete) is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional specification contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional specification must describe the nature of the invention and be accompanied by drawings if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional spec is a short description enabling provisional protection; drawings required where necessary (see rules on drawings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete specification contents and form
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete specification must particularly describe and ascertain the nature of the invention and in what manner it is to be performed, must commence with the title and must end with a distinct statement of the invention claimed, and must be accompanied by drawings if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises particularity and sufficiency of disclosure: must teach how to perform the invention and include a clear claim; format requirements (title, end with claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's duties on referral
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller shall refer every application to an examiner who shall ascertain and report whether the nature of the invention has been fairly described, and whether the application, specification, and drawings have been prepared in the prescribed manner, and whether the title sufficiently indicates the subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner assesses sufficiency of description, formal compliance, and adequacy of title; report to Comptroller drives further action (acceptance/refusal/require amendment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusal or requirement to amend on examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner reports that the nature of the invention is not fairly described, or that the application, specification, or drawings have not been prepared in the prescribed manner, or that the title does not sufficiently indicate the subject-matter, the Comptroller may refuse to accept the application or require amendment before proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may be required to correct formal or substantive defects; refusal or conditional acceptance may affect effective date (application may bear date from compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from Comptroller's refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Comptroller refuses to accept an application or requires an amendment, the applicant may appeal from his decision to the law officer, who may hear applicant and Comptroller and make orders determining whether and on what conditions the application shall be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural remedy and review by law officer; hearing may be ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for lodging complete specification
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant does not leave a complete specification with his application, he may leave it at any subsequent time within nine months from the date of application; unless a complete specification is left within that time the application shall be deemed to be abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nine-month limit (Comptroller empowered to grant limited further time under later amending provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance timeframe for complete specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a complete specification is accepted within twelve months from the date of application (save in case of an appeal having been lodged), the application shall, at the expiration of those twelve months, become void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner reports are confidential; acceptance timeframe creates a deadline for acceptance after which application is void unless appeal is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison requirement after provisional specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete specification is left after a provisional specification the examiner must ascertain whether the complete specification has been prepared in the prescribed manner and whether the invention described in the complete specification is substantially the same as that described in the provisional specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete spec cannot introduce a substantially different invention from the provisional; otherwise Comptroller may refuse acceptance until amended; appeal available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement and public inspection on acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: On acceptance of the complete specification the Comptroller shall advertise the acceptance; and the application and specification(s), with drawings if any, shall be open to public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance triggers publication for public inspection and starts opposition window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to grant — permitted grounds and time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may at any time within two months from the date of advertisement of acceptance give notice of opposition to the grant of the patent on the ground that the applicant obtained the invention from him, or that the invention has been patented in this country on an application of prior date, or that the complete specification describes or claims an invention other than that described in the provisional specification (and such other invention is subject of an intervening application by the opponent), but on no other ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition is tightly circumscribed to named grounds and must be given within two months; procedures for hearing and law officer determination are set out; law officer may obtain expert assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealing of patent on grant or determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no opposition, or if opposition determination is in favour of grant, the Comptroller shall cause a patent to be sealed with the seal of the Patent Office; a patent shall be sealed as soon as may be and not after the expiration of fifteen months from the date of application, except in specified cases (appeal, opposition, death of applicant etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sealing confers full patent; there are statutory deadlines for sealing subject to enumerated exceptions (appeal, applicant death permitted delays).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of patent and limitation on infringement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall be dated and sealed as of the day of the application; but no proceedings shall be taken in respect of an infringement committed before the publication of the complete specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent retroactively dated to application but enforcement for pre-publication infringing acts is limited until publication of complete specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional protection between application and sealing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application has been accepted, the invention may during the period between the date of application and the date of sealing be used and published without prejudice to the patent to be granted; such protection is referred to as provisional protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes conservative interim rights and public use: applicant has certain protections following acceptance, but formal enforcement may be limited until sealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of acceptance of complete specification before sealing
rubrics_metrics.description: After acceptance of a complete specification and until the date of sealing or expiration of the time for sealing, the applicant shall have the like privileges and rights as if a patent had been sealed on the date of acceptance; provided that an applicant shall not be entitled to institute any proceeding for infringement until a patent has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance confers quasi-rights but no ability to sue for infringement until the patent is actually granted (sealed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial extent and statutory term of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent when sealed shall have effect throughout the extent of the United Kingdom and the Isle of Man; the term limited in every patent shall be fourteen years from its date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines territorial scope and default statutory term (subject to payments and extensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to pay prescribed fees and enlargement for accidental default
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall cease if the patentee fails to make the prescribed payments within the prescribed times; but if by accident, mistake or inadvertence the patentee fails to make a prescribed payment he may apply for enlargement of time (on payment of prescribed fee not exceeding ten pounds) and the Comptroller may enlarge time up to three months subject to conditions; courts may in some cases refuse damages for infringements occurring during the unpaid period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides remedy for unintentional non-payment but with limits (three months max enlargement) and potential loss of damages for intervening infringements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to amend specification (disclaimer, correction, explanation)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or a patentee may, by request in writing left at the Patent Office, seek leave to amend his specification (including drawings) by way of disclaimer, correction, or explanation, stating the nature of the amendment and reasons; the request and proposed amendment shall be advertised, and opposition may be given within one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment procedure is formal, advertised and subject to opposition and appeal to law officer; advertising gives third parties notice and opportunity to oppose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on amendments — no enlargement or substantive change
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment shall be allowed that would make the specification, as amended, claim an invention substantially larger than, or substantially different from, the invention claimed by the specification as it stood before amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core substantive limitation: amendments cannot broaden or change the claimed invention materially; leave to amend conclusive except in case of fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendment while infringement or revocation proceedings are pending
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions allowing amendment do not apply when, and so long as, any action for infringement or proceeding for revocation of a patent is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents use of Patent Office amendment routes to influence ongoing litigation; court may, however, order application for leave to amend and stay trial (see sec. 19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court power to permit amendment in litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action for infringement or proceeding for revocation the Court or a judge may at any time order that the patentee shall, subject to such terms as to costs and otherwise as the Court or judge may impose, be at liberty to apply at the Patent Office for leave to amend his specification by way of disclaimer, and may direct that in the meantime the trial or hearing shall be postponed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court has supervisory power to allow amendments during litigation but may impose terms and stay proceedings to avoid prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on damages after amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment by way of disclaimer, correction or explanation has been allowed, no damages shall be given in any action in respect of the use of the invention before the amendment unless the patentee establishes to the satisfaction of the Court that his original claim was framed in good faith and with reasonable skill and knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects defendants from retroactive damages when claims are narrowed unless patentee acted in good faith and with competence in original drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licence grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on petition, it is proved to the Board of Trade that by reason of the default of a patentee to grant licences on reasonable terms (a) the patent is not being worked in the United Kingdom; or (b) the reasonable requirements of the public with respect to the invention cannot be supplied; or (c) any person is prevented from working or using to the best advantage an invention of which he is possessed, the Board may order the patentee to grant licences on such terms as the Board deems just.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board of Trade can impose compulsory licences for public interest or non-working; orders may be enforced by mandamus; Board considers nature of invention and circumstances in deciding terms (royalties, security, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of Patents — entries and evidentiary effect
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be kept at the Patent Office a Register of Patents wherein shall be entered names and addresses of grantees, notifications of assignments and transmissions, of licences under patents, and of amendments, extensions and revocations and such other prescribed matters; the register shall be prima-facie evidence of any matters directed to be inserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register functions as official record and prima facie proof of recorded facts; copies of deeds/licences must be supplied for filing in the prescribed manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and Board of Trade authority
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be paid in respect of instruments described in the Second Schedule the fees mentioned therein, and such other fees as may be prescribed by the Board of Trade with Treasury sanction; the Board may, with Treasury consent, from time to time reduce any of those fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory fees govern many transactions; Board/Treasury can adjust fees subject to procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of term by Her Majesty in Council (petition and criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may petition Her Majesty in Council (at least six months before expiry) to extend his patent term; the Judicial Committee shall consider the nature and merits of the invention in relation to the public, the profits made by the patentee, and all circumstances; if inadequately remunerated the Committee may report and Council may extend the term up to seven or in exceptional cases fourteen years or order a new patent with conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension petitions involve advertisement, caveats by third parties, hearing before Judicial Committee, discretion as to costs and extension length; Committee weighs public interest and patentee remuneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation proceedings and available grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Revocation of a patent may be obtained on petition to the Court; every ground on which a patent might previously be repealed by scire facias shall be available, and revocation grounds may be used as a defence in infringement actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes revocation by petition in court as the remedy; enumerates who may present petitions and preserves traditional grounds as available defences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may present petition for revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for revocation may be presented by (a) the Attorney-General in England or Ireland, or the Lord Advocate in Scotland; (b) any person authorised by those officers; (c) any person alleging the patent was obtained in fraud of his rights; (d) any person alleging he (or a predecessor) was the true inventor; (e) any person alleging prior manufacture, use or sale in the realm before the date of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines standing to seek revocation including state officers, alleged true inventors, and prior users/manufacturers/sellers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars required with revocation petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The plaintiff must deliver with his petition particulars of the objections on which he means to rely, and no evidence shall, except by leave of the Court or a judge, be admitted in proof of any objection of which particulars are not so delivered; particulars may be amended by leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement to specify grounds and particulars upfront to ensure fair notice; Court controls late evidence and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief where patent revoked for fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent has been revoked on the ground of fraud, the Comptroller may, on the application of the true inventor made in accordance with the Act, grant to him a patent in lieu of and having the same date as the date of revocation of the patent so revoked; but the patent so granted shall cease on the expiration of the term for which the revoked patent was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides remediation to true inventor when patent revoked for fraud, but new patent's remaining term is limited to original term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patent against the Crown and Crown use
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall have the like effect against Her Majesty and her successors as it has against a subject; but Crown departments may, by themselves, agents or contractors, at any time after application, use the invention for services of the Crown on terms to be agreed with approval of the Treasury, or if no agreement, on terms settled by the Treasury after hearing parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents bind the Crown but Crown retains use rights on agreed or Treasury-determined terms for public service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of assessors in patent proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action or proceeding for infringement or revocation the Court may, and shall on request of either party, call in the aid of an assessor specially qualified and try or hear the case wholly or partially with his assistance; the action shall be tried without a jury unless Court otherwise directs; Court of Appeal and Judicial Committee may also call assessors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessor assistance is available to provide technical expertise; remuneration to be determined and paid as Court orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars in infringement proceedings — delivery and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action for infringement the plaintiff must deliver particulars of the breaches complained of with his statement of claim (or by court order), and the defendant must deliver particulars of objections with his defence; if the defendant disputes validity he must state grounds and, if want of novelty, time and place of prior publication or user alleged; evidence of unparticularised allegations is inadmissible without leave; particulars may be amended; taxation of costs will take particulars into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict particularisation requirements govern evidence admissibility and cost consequences; ensures parties provide specifics of allegations early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court powers for injunction, inspection and accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action for infringement the Court or a judge may, on application of either party, make orders for an injunction, inspection or account, impose such terms, and give directions as the Court or judge thinks fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedial and interlocutory powers to preserve rights and obtain disclosure/relief in infringement litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of validity in issue and costs consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court or a judge may certify that the validity of the patent came in question; if so, in any subsequent infringement action the plaintiff obtaining a final order in his favour shall have his full costs as between solicitor and client unless the trial court certifies he ought not to have them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification shifts adverse cost rules to favour successful plaintiff in later actions where validity issue was previously raised, deterring repeated questionable suits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection from groundless threats of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person claiming to be patentee threatens others by circulars, advertisements or otherwise with legal proceedings in respect of alleged manufacture, use, sale or purchase, any person aggrieved may bring action for injunction and recover damages if threatened activity was not in fact infringement; this section does not apply if the person making threats with due diligence commences and prosecutes an action for infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides remedy for victims of baseless enforcement threats, but protects good-faith assertion of rights if followed by diligent prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of patent and single invention rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent may be in the form in the First Schedule and shall be granted for one invention only, but may contain more than one claim; it shall not be competent for any person in an action or other proceeding to object to a patent on the ground that it comprises more than one invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent should be for one invention though multiple claims allowed; courts will not entertain objections merely that patent comprises more than one invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by legal representative after applicant's death
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person possessed of an invention dies without making application, application for a patent may be made by his legal representative within six months of decease, containing a declaration that he believes the deceased to be the true and first inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure protects inventors' estates and allows posthumous applications by representatives within six-month window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent not invalidated by certain fraudulent or intervening acts
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent granted to the true and first inventor shall not be invalidated by an application in fraud of him, or by provisional protection obtained on such fraudulent application, or by any use or publication of the invention subsequent to that fraudulent application during the period of provisional protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects rights of true and first inventors against certain fraudulent filings and intervening public uses occurring during provisional protection period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of patent for parts of UK
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may assign his patent for any place in or part of the United Kingdom or Isle of Man as effectually as if the patent were originally granted to extend to that place or part only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows territorially-limited assignments/transfer of rights within statutory geography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate patent where original lost or destroyed
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is lost or destroyed, or its non-production is accounted for to the satisfaction of the Comptroller, the Comptroller may at any time cause a duplicate thereof to be sealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative remedy for lost/destroyed originals to restore documentary proof of patent.
